messages:
release-manager: Heads up — canary observed a cosign/signature mismatch on the offline bundle we pushed to customer-rc at 09:02 UTC. Notifying ops.

deploy-bot: [canary-report] installer-canary-3: checksum_failed on bundle.tar.gz (exit 43) :warning: see /artifacts/canary/installer-canary-3/logs.txt

olivia: I pulled the bundle from the canary node and ran a verify:
```
$ cosign verify-blob --signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
verification for bundle.tar.gz: FAIL: signature not valid
```

mike: :eyes: that suggests the manifest was re-signed with a different key or the signature step used a different submanifest. Did packaging run again during the window?

sam: Packaging pipeline shows two signer jobs for the same epoch: `packager-sign-v1` and `packager-sign-retry` within 6m of each other. The second one used key alias `projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/release/cryptoKeys/signer-v2`.

anya: If both got published to the artifact mirror, downstream installers could pick the wrong submanifest digest. Recommend we pause rollout and either revert canary to the previous signed bundle or re-sign to match the published manifest.

carla: Agreed. We should not advance a full rollout until we have a cleanly signed artifact and reproducible checksums. What are rollback criteria?

release-manager: Quick decision: pause remaining canaries, rollback installer-canary-3 to last-good tag `v1.4.3-rc2`. Then create a hotfix pipeline to produce a single authoritative signed bundle, run full verification and checksum republish.

mike: Commands for ops to run:
```
# rollback canary to previous signed bundle
deploybot rollback --target installer-canary-3 --image-tag v1.4.3-rc2 --reason "cosign mismatch"
# verify artifact after rollback
sha256sum bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz
cosign verify-blob --signature bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.sig bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz
```

olivia: I'll run the verification and post results. If verify passes, we can let canary stabilize and then schedule republish during the next 2h change window.

sam: Notes for republish:
- lock packager so only one signer job runs (single KMS alias)
- regenerate submanifest and compute checksums
- cosign sign with `signer-v1` KMS alias (security will confirm)
- publish manifest with epoch bump in installer metadata

anya: Security check: we need KMS auditlogs for the signer operation and to confirm no key rotation happened mid-packaging. Adding INF-4567.

carla: Also update release notes: add an entry under Triage -> Packaging: "Canary detected signature mismatch; rolled back to v1.4.3-rc2 while we re-sign authoritative bundle."

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: rollback-7894 started, ETA ~2m.

olivia: verify after rollback:
```
$ cosign verify-blob --signature bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.sig bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz
verification for bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz: OK
$ sha256sum bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz
54b1c9...  bundle-v1.4.3-rc2.tar.gz
```

release-manager: Good. Hold full rollout until republish is complete and security signs off. I'll update the release channel and the release checklist. INF-4567 assigned, timeline: republish attempt within 45m change window.

mike: If republish fails, fallback plan is to freeze release and schedule full repackage tomorrow morning with oncall support.

olivia: I'll attach logs and cosign outputs to INF-4567.

carla: Thanks everyone. I'll push the release notes patch and tag the incident for postmortem if needed. :white_check_mark:
